prompt:
LOW-LEVEL PHOTOGRAPHIC RESTORATION ONLY. This is an image-preservation task, not a creative generation, face restoration, beauty retouching, or reinterpretation task. Use the input image as the only ground truth.

HIGHEST-PRIORITY IDENTITY LOCK: Treat every face and the entire head region in the source image as an immutable, protected region. Preserve each face exactly as it appears in the input. The output face must remain precisely aligned with the source and must retain the same identity, facial geometry, proportions, expression, gaze, head pose, asymmetry, age, skin texture, hairline, hairstyle, and all visible distinguishing features. Do not synthesize, regenerate, reconstruct, reinterpret, beautify, retouch, reshape, correct, sharpen, smooth, or add new details to any face. Do not attempt to recover missing or unclear facial details. Preserve naturally blurred, compressed, partially hidden, or low-detail facial features exactly as they are instead of inventing replacements.

Inside every facial and head region, permit only resolution resampling and the same uniform global gamma, exposure, and white-balance correction applied to the entire photograph. No local facial enhancement, selective sharpening, skin cleanup, eye enhancement, teeth enhancement, portrait relighting, or generative detail restoration is permitted. Facial identity preservation has absolute priority over sharpness, detail enhancement, and overall image quality. If any requested enhancement could alter a face, skip that enhancement in the facial region.

Preserve the original composition, framing, crop, perspective, geometry, object placement, body shape, clothing, background, lighting direction, and scene content. Do not add, remove, replace, or reposition anything.

Upscale the photograph using conservative, source-faithful resampling. Improve technical quality outside the protected facial regions by reducing compression artifacts, pixelation, color noise, and mild blur while retaining authentic textures and original edge structure. Do not invent details that are not visibly supported by the source image.

Correct the global gamma, exposure, tonal balance, and white balance. Recover usable shadow and highlight information conservatively, neutralize unwanted color casts, and maintain natural contrast, realistic colors, and smooth tonal transitions. Apply these corrections uniformly without changing local facial lighting or facial appearance.

The final output must look like the exact same original photograph at a higher resolution with corrected gamma and white balance. It must not look regenerated. Every person must remain immediately and unmistakably identical to the source. When preservation and enhancement conflict, always choose preservation.
